grade_reason: Eight web searches found no statement by Brent Taylor about AI risk since 1 January 2025; the only AI-adjacent material is about data center legislation and campaign attacks over it, which is outside this project's scope.
notes: All 8 searches ran; none was refused. The only AI-adjacent item: a Tennessee Lookout report (24 September 2026, https://tennesseelookout.com/2026/09/24/democratic-leaning-pac-goes-after-republican-congressional-candidate-over-data-centers/) says a Democratic-leaning PAC attacked Taylor for taking money from AI and data center companies and for passing Senate Bill 2128 on data center power; per the search summary Taylor replied that he passed the only data center regulation in the legislature that year, one that keeps companies from raising utility rates. This was seen only as a search-result paraphrase (the page and its newsfromthestates.com copy returned 403 Forbidden), so no quote was taken. Even if confirmed it would be level D (data centers, electricity bills), so a reviewer could reasonably change the grade from none to D. Several search results concerned Bret Taylor (OpenAI chair), a different person; they were ignored. As a state senator he was not in the House in 2025-2026, so he could not co-sponsor the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act or sign the House letters. No campaign site with policy pages was found. Search was not exhaustive for local debates, interviews or candidate questionnaires.
